newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo sees restaurants spun off by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo sees restaurants spun off by yr-end.

text.p: PepsiCo chairman Roger Enrico said he Friday expects the spin-off of its restaurant business to shareholders will be complete by the end of 1997.
PepsiCo announced last night it will become solely a packaged goods business -- beverages and snack foods -- with the transaction.
The new company, to be composed of the KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell restaurant chains, is expected to carry an investment grade debt rating, he said.
The deal was not made in anticipation of any acquisitions by PepsiCo, he said in a conference with analysts.
Enrico also said PepsiCo expects to divest its New Zealand restaurant operation through an initial public offering.
The restaurant division accounted for 37 percent of PepsiCo's $30.42 billion in 1995 revenue and 24 percent of the $1.61 billion net income.
The spin-off is expected to be tax-free to shareholders.
